documents.title: Phone Call: Rash
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pt called my line early. Since yesterday morning, itchy raised red welts across her stomach, back and both arms. Says individual spots fade within hours but new ones pop up elsewhere. Sent photos through the portal, look like hives. No lip, tongue or eyelid swelling. No throat tightness, no wheeze or trouble breathing. Feels well otherwise. No new meds, foods, detergents or recent illness she can think of.

Dermatology had a cancellation tomorrow at 9, booked her in so they can see it while it's active.

Reviewed red flags: any swelling of lips/tongue, throat tightness, trouble breathing or lightheadedness -> 911/ED, don't wait for the appointment. She understands.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT DERMATOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 04/25/2025
Requested by: primary care physician
Reason for consultation: widespread pruritic eruption

HISTORY: 26-year-old woman seen on short notice with a two-day history of intensely pruritic, raised red lesions over the trunk and both arms. The lesions are transient. Any single lesion clears in less than 24 hours, though fresh ones continue to appear at other sites. She has had no preceding illness, has started no new drug or supplement, and has not changed her diet. She denies lip or tongue swelling, abdominal pain and shortness of breath.

Past medical history: noncontributory.
Medications: none.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: mother, seasonal allergic rhinitis; father, asthma.
Social history: graphic designer. Never smoker. Alcohol 1-2 drinks per month.

EXAMINATION: Vital signs within normal limits. Numerous sharply marginated erythematous plaques of variable size over the trunk and upper extremities, several surrounded by a pale halo. Oral mucosa uninvolved. Breathing comfortably, no distress.

LABORATORY (drawn at this visit): CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel and TSH within normal limits. Serum tryptase 4.1 ng/mL, not elevated.

IMPRESSION: Acute urticaria. No precipitant identified on history.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
1. Cetirizine 10 mg by mouth once daily for 14 days.
2. Seek emergency care for any lip, tongue or throat swelling or difficulty breathing.
3. Should hives recur, we would suggest referral to allergy and immunology.
4. Follow up with dermatology as needed.

Dermatology attending

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derm consult from 4/25 reviewed. Acute urticaria, no trigger. CBC, CMP, TSH normal, tryptase 4.1. On cetirizine 10 daily x 2 wk. Will check in with her by message.

documents.title: Dermatology Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Natalia, I have the dermatology note now. Your bloodwork from Friday was all normal, including the tryptase, which is the test that would point toward a mast cell problem. So this looks like plain acute hives. How are the spots doing on the cetirizine?

documents.title: RE: Dermatology Visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Way better, just a couple small ones on my arm today and the itching is mostly gone. The cetirizine makes me a little sleepy if I take it in the morning so I switched to bedtime.

documents.title: Hives Gone
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! No new hives since last Thursday. Do I keep taking the cetirizine until the 2 weeks are up or can I stop?

documents.title: RE: Hives Gone
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news. Finish out the 14 days the dermatologist gave you, then stop. If they return after you finish, message me.

documents.title: Allergy and Immunology Consultation
documents.author: allergy and immunology
documents.body:
ALLERGY & IMMUNOLOGY | NEW CONSULT
Visit date: 12/24/2025
Referred by: primary care

CC: hives x 24 hours.

HPI: Ms. Gillespie is a 26 y/o graphic designer referred for itchy, raised, red wheals over the trunk and both arms that began yesterday morning. She had an episode of the same appearance in April 2025, evaluated by dermatology, which resolved on a two-week course of cetirizine. Before this flare she had no infection, no new medication and no dietary change. No fever, joint pain, abdominal pain or breathing difficulty.

Prior workup (April 2025, dermatology): CBC, CMP, TSH normal; tryptase 4.1 ng/mL.

Meds: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: mother with seasonal allergic rhinitis; father with asthma.
SHx: never smoker; alcohol 1-2 drinks/month.

PE: Vitals WNL. Skin: well-demarcated wheals of varying size on trunk and arms, blanching with pressure. No other skin changes. HEENT, chest, heart and abdomen normal. No lip or tongue swelling.

ASSESSMENT: Acute urticaria, second episode. Each episode short-lived, no identifiable trigger by history, normal labs in April. This does not meet criteria for chronic urticaria.

PLAN:
- No further testing needed at this point.
- Cetirizine 10 mg PO daily as needed for hives; during a flare, take it every day until it settles. Rx sent.
- Return to clinic if hives occur most days for 6 weeks.
- Lip or tongue swelling or any difficulty breathing: emergency care.

Allergy & Immunology
